edits.text: - Determines whether the continuation forces reinterpreting who or what acted, or whether an event occurred — for example by introducing negation, restriction, a new scope, or by changing a referent or the factual status. If the right side can reverse or invalidate the earlier inference, the cut scores poorly on this judgement.

- Measures whether translating the halves separately loses essential dependencies or attachments. Damage includes a noun left without its modifier or 'of' phrase, a verb separated from its object/particle, stranded possessives or prepositional attachments, or modifiers whose scope becomes unclear. Watch relative clauses, subordinators, negation/auxiliary scope, coordination inside phrases, clause‑introducing heads, and narrow‑focus adverbials — these often make earlier material provisional.

Before assigning Contra, check whether the right side supplies the main predicate or any scope‑changing element (negation, restriction/contrastive particle, numeric quantifier/comparative, or other material that can reverse or refine the left inference). If the continuation completes or can reverse the left fragment's truth or role, treat the left stretch as provisional: raise Contra substantially and lower the target accordingly.

Head–complement cohesion rule: treat any cut that separates a content head (noun, verb, adjective) from an essential complement or prepositional modifier as low‑cohesion unless the right side is clearly parenthetical or optional. If cutting would leave a head without its required complement (e.g. 'container' separated from 'of X', or a verb without its object/particle), set Cohesion much lower and avoid that cut.
